intro: A quiet Thursday with thin retailer and book news. The main threads are rules on affiliate tracking, AI shopping agents getting blocked or fed product catalogues, and ChatGPT taking a bigger share of search.

must_reads.title: APMA Sets Out Case for UK Affiliate Tracking Reform
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: The UK affiliate trade body wants a narrow privacy-law exemption so the data used to confirm a sale and pay the commission doesn't need cookie consent. Its point is simple: the shop gets the sale but the publisher loses the commission when the tracking link fails. How tracking is regulated shapes how reliably every affiliate link gets credit.

must_reads.title: Bot protection blocks Blend's AI shopping agent at 29 of 200 retailers
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: A test found 29 of 200 retailers blocked an AI shopping agent, with big retailers far more likely to say no. If AI agents can't always reach store pages, the path from a recommendation to a purchase gets patchier, and working links to the right store matter more.

must_reads.title: Microsoft Clarity puts Shopify and WooCommerce products in Copilot and Bing
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Microsoft now lets Shopify and WooCommerce stores send their product catalogue straight into Copilot and Bing. Another AI assistant is building its own shopping shelf, so shoppers find products in more places than the usual store sites.

must_reads.title: ChatGPT reaches a fifth of Google search volume as Taboola blames AI
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: OpenAI says ChatGPT handles about a fifth of Google's search-like volume, and Taboola blamed AI summaries for a 6.9% revenue fall. Fewer clicks from search means publishers and creators need every click they do get to land in the right store.

must_reads.title: Instagram tries to entice long-form creators
must_reads.why: Why it matters for Geniuslink: Instagram is offering one-off payouts and better placement to win long-form creators from YouTube. Platforms are competing hard for the same creators, which is a reminder that creators spread their audience across many apps rather than living on one.
